notes: New state. Eastern Umbria and the Adriatic slopes from the Iron Age (900, confidence 1) to the Roman conquest 'by approximately 260 BC'; the coast goes to the Senones c. 390. The roman-republic dossier has no gain for Umbria (its shapes grow over 301-291 and 281-271 without naming it); the 260 dissolve hands the land to Rome as allied cities. Wikidata unverified. Revised 2026-10-19 after review: keyframes added; the dossier follows roman-republic's vassal model (vassal_start 260, vassal_end 90 with citizenship, as /ledger/38 and /135) and ends in 90 instead of 260, with no loss to Rome at 260; the Pesaro-Ancona strip is claimed by both this dossier (Senones page: 'displacing the Umbrians') and, on the Picentes page, by Picenum ('occupied Picenum north of the Esino'): it is drawn once, as Umbrian, and picentes drops its 390 loss; the Iguvine Tablets page was opened for the thin capital and does not call Iguvium a capital.
